response.corpus: "AI and the legal profession" — 1,501 curated published sources (scholarship, industry evidence, primary legal materials and practitioner interview transcripts, 1949–2026), structured by the Insight Bridge pipeline.
notes: Source counts are NOT prevalence: this is a curated evidence base, not a survey of the field. Never read "N sources say X" as a measurement of how common X is.

Positions are relative to each cluster's own proposition — they measure stance-toward-a-framing, not absolute agreement. 424 of 9777 source stances push back (Redirects/Opposes/Mixed); see contested_topics.
The grouping tree has 2 generation(s): 5 families over 46 themes over 369 topics. Ids of every generation work with topics_in_supercluster.
Era is ORDINAL and derived from publication year: Foundations (pre-2015) → Automation debate (2015-2022) → Generative shock (2023-2024) → Adoption at scale (2025) → Current wave (2026).
124 sources have restricted distribution: their syntheses, stances and key points are present but their passage text is not served and search_passages never returns them.

Voice coverage varies widely; check each cluster's own voice mix (get_topic, voice_profile) before weighing corroboration. Transcript sources are auto-generated captions; proper nouns are sometimes garbled.
